claim: The positive effect of a brand's perceived value on brand loyalty is significantly weaker for a new mobile technology generation than for an existing one, meaning preference formed under one technology paradigm only partially transfers to the same brand under a new paradigm.
stance_target: the assumption that Apple's brand-preference-based loyalty would carry over largely intact if AI relocated the primary interface away from the phone
scope_conditions: Structural equation model on n=514 mobile phone users aged 18-35 in Singapore, comparing 2.5G (existing) vs 3G (new) technology generations, same respondents/brands
quoted_support: H4 states that the effect of perceived value on mobile device brand loyalty is more positive for the existing mobile technology generation than the new generation... the change in chi-squared with this constraint is significant: chi-sq(1) = 7.17, p < .01... the coefficient indicated in Table 4 is more positive for the existing generation than the new generation (.61 vs. .31).
time_period: data collected pre-2013 (2.5G/3G transition era), published 2013/2014

claim: Perceived benevolence (trust that the manufacturer cares about the customer's welfare) becomes a significantly stronger positive driver of brand loyalty for a new technology generation than for an existing one, reversing sign from negative to positive.
stance_target: trust/relational bonds toward a brand are more transferable across a technology-paradigm shift than value-based preference is
scope_conditions: Same SEM study, n=514, Singapore, 2.5G vs 3G
quoted_support: H5 states that the effect of perceived benevolence on mobile device brand loyalty is more positive for the new mobile technology generation than for the existing generation... the coefficient for the effect of perceived benevolence is more positive for the new generation than the existing generation (.18 vs. -.18).

claim: Early adopters of a mobile technology rely more on perceived value (rational utility comparison) to form brand loyalty, while late adopters rely more on brand satisfaction (satisficing), and this asymmetry holds regardless of technology generation.
stance_target: segmentation of loyalty drivers by adopter type, relevant to which Apple customer segments would be most exposed if a new AI-interface paradigm arrives
quoted_support: the effect of perceived value is more positive for early adopters than late adopters, supporting H1... the effect of brand satisfaction on mobile device brand loyalty is more positive for late than early adopters.
numbers: interaction coefficient perceived value x adopter type = -.38, p<.05
interaction coefficient brand satisfaction x adopter type = .40, p<.01

claim: The mobile phone industry has historically exhibited high levels of brand switching among consumers, motivating research into what drives brand loyalty at the device-brand level.
stance_target: baseline context that brand switching in mobile devices is common, not rare
scope_conditions: General mobile device market, citing Stremersch, Muller, and Peres 2010
quoted_support: Because the mobile phone industry exhibits high levels of brand switching among consumers (Stremersch, Muller, and Peres 2010) and because customer loyalty is typically mismanaged (Reinartz and Kumar 2002), marketers of mobile devices are concerned about managing customer brand loyalty.

claim: 84% of iPhone buyers surveyed by GfK in 2011 felt emotionally attached to the brand and indicated they would choose iPhone again.
stance_target: historical baseline of Apple's brand attachment strength, for comparison against post-DMA/post-AI-interface durability
quoted_support: In the mobile device context, 84 percent of iPhone buyers surveyed by market research firm Gfk felt attached to this brand and indicated that they would choose iPhone again (Gfk 2011).

claim: Consumers perceive greater uncertainty and risk when adopting a new technology generation than when repurchasing within an existing one, which shifts the basis of loyalty from value comparison toward trust in the manufacturer.
stance_target: mechanism explaining why an AI-interface paradigm shift could weaken Apple's value-based loyalty advantage while trust-based loyalty could persist or even matter more
scope_conditions: General technology adoption theory, mobile device context
quoted_support: a new mobile technology generation involves new or improved features and applications of new technology. Because of the 'newness' of these features, hidden hazards... may not have been identified and potential performance problems may still exist... consumers may perceive higher performance risks when adopting a new mobile generation than an existing generation.
